title: The Script, Line by Line
summary: Every line in order, and the step that breaks on a third of real calls.

lines.speaker: agent
lines.text: Hey, good morning (Customer's Name), this is _______, I'm with America's Health on a recorded line. We were just giving you a quick call today about the Medicaid meal service for you and your family. I just need to confirm you ARE still receiving Medicaid, correct?

blocks.html: Four things in one breath: who you're speaking to, your company, the recorded line, and what the call is about — then straight into the Medicaid question.

blocks.title: Don't lose the recorded line
blocks.html: It's missing from the opening on about 1 in 20 real calls, and skipped or rushed on far more. It costs you two seconds.

blocks.question: Which belongs in the opening?
choices: That the call is on a recorded line
blocks.explanation: Name, company, recorded line, what the call is about.

lines.speaker: agent
lines.text: Okay perfect, and you're still in (Customer's Borough), with the zip code (Customer's Zip Code), correct?

blocks.html: One sentence, two facts. The borough decides whether they're in the service area; the ZIP goes to the screener.

blocks.title: The ZIP is the most skipped verification
blocks.html: Missing on 24.7% of real calls, and rushed on another 18.7%. It's in the same sentence as the borough — there's no reason for it to go missing except speed.

blocks.question: The consumer gives the borough but not the ZIP. What do you do?
choices: Ask for the ZIP before continuing
Move on — borough is the important one
Read them the ZIP from the screen and move on

lessons.title: Permission to transfer — the broken step

lines.speaker: agent
lines.text: Perfect, that's everything I need. The screener is coming on the line now to help you set that up, once that's finished, they'll have you on your way, okay?

lines.speaker: note
lines.text: AFFIRM — MUST GET PERMISSION TO TRANSFER

blocks.title: A third of real calls skip this entirely
blocks.html: Permission was never obtained on 32.3% of calls, and rushed on another 19.9%. It is the single biggest procedural gap on this campaign — 446 calls in the sample were transferred with no okay from the consumer.
The word “okay?” is in the script for a reason. Say it, then stop talking until you hear an answer. Silence is not permission, and neither is the consumer still being on the line.

blocks.question: You say “…they'll have you on your way, okay?” and hear nothing. What now?
choices: Ask again and wait for an answer

lines.speaker: agent
lines.text: Hey agent, I have (Customer's Name) in (Customer's Borough), the zip code for them is (Customer's Zip). Can you take the call from here? Okay, I'll drop the line and let you two finish up, you both have a great day!

blocks.html: Three facts in the handoff: who, which borough, which ZIP. This is the step agents are best at — 83% do it properly — so it's mostly a matter of not letting it slip.

blocks.question: What goes in the handoff?
blocks.explanation: All three, then wait for them to engage before dropping.

blocks.html: When someone doesn't qualify, there is one approved line:

blocks.objection: No Medicaid / copays / outside the boroughs
blocks.response: Oh there must have been a mistake, thank you for your time, have a great day.
blocks.coach_note: Warm, short, and then end the call. No arguing, no trying to find a way around it, no transferring to see what the screener says.

blocks.title: A DQ is a correct outcome, not a loss
blocks.html: 169 consumers in the sample should have been DQ'd. 99 were caught. 38 were transferred anyway — mostly people who said plainly they don't have Medicaid. Catching a DQ is a good call; transferring one is the failure.

blocks.question: “No, I don't have Medicaid.” What do you do?
choices: Transfer and let the screener decide
Read the DQ line and end the call
Ask if they have Medicare instead
blocks.explanation: Read the line, code it DQ, move on.

questions.question: What must be in your opening?
Which step is skipped most often?
questions.explanation: 32.3% — the biggest gap on the campaign.

questions.question: Silence after the transfer ask means…
The ZIP is skipped on roughly…
What three facts go in the handoff?
A consumer doesn't qualify. You should…
choices: Read the DQ line and end
questions.explanation: The approved DQ line, then end.

questions.question: How many consumers in the sample were transferred despite not qualifying?
questions.explanation: 38 of the 169 who should have been DQ'd.

questions.question: When can you drop the line on the handoff?
choices: Once the screener and consumer are talking
As soon as the screener answers
